footer.tagline: Kithwall is free and open source. No ads. No tracking.
landing.title: Your people. Your space. Sealed.
landing.lede: A private social network for your family, your friends and the circles you belong to. Everything you share is encrypted on your device, so nobody can read it — not even us.
landing.ctaNote: Free forever. No phone number, no email needed, no password to remember.
landing.p1Body: Posts, photos, messages, names and reactions are encrypted on your device before they leave it. We only ever store sealed data.
landing.p2Body: No advertisers, no analytics, no data brokers. Nothing about you is for sale, because there is no one to sell it to.
landing.p3Body: A chronological feed from people you know, no public like counts, and a clear “you're all caught up”. No algorithm deciding what you see.
landing.p4Body: No phone number, no contact upload, email optional. We keep logs short and ask only for what Kithwall needs to work.
landing.p5Body: Disappearing messages on, read receipts off, your profile visible only to your connections. Relax any of it whenever you like.
landing.p6Body: Open-source code, one-tap export, verifiable safety numbers, and a live page showing exactly what our server knows about you.
landing.s1Body: Warm, Minimal or Bold — in light or dark. Change it any time.
landing.s2Body: Unlock with your face, fingerprint or screen lock. Your keys are made on your device. There's no password.
landing.s3Body: Share a link or a QR code with the people you actually know. We never upload your contacts.
landing.stylesBody: Three styles, each with a light and a dark version. Pick one when you join; switch whenever you like.
landing.donateBody: Kithwall is free for everyone, with no paid tier and no paywall. It will be funded by donations from the people who use it. Donations aren’t open yet, but there are other ways to help.

donate.lede: Kithwall is free and open source. There are no ads, no tracking and no paid tier, and there never will be. It’s meant to be funded by the people who use it.
donate.closedBody: We aren’t taking money yet. When donations open, the ways to give will appear on this page. Until then, the ways to help below make the biggest difference.

help.title: Help Center
help.lede: Answers about Kithwall 2: passkeys, recovery, connections, circles, stories and staying safe.
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.a1: A private social network for the people you actually know: family, friends and the circles you belong to. Everything you post, send or store is **end-to-end encrypted** on your device. There are no ads, no tracking and no algorithm: Home shows posts from your connections and circles, newest first.
help.start.q2: How do I find my people?
help.start.a2: There's no contact upload. Share your **invite link or QR code** from [Connections](/people?tab=invite), or look someone up by their exact @handle. When someone joins with your link, you get a connection request from them.
help.start.a3: **Home** (stories and your feed), **Circles** (groups with their own feed, chat, albums, events and notes), **Messages**, **Activity** (notifications and requests) and **You** (your profile, albums, notes, events and settings).
help.signin.title: Passkeys and signing in
help.signin.a1: A passkey lets you sign in with your face, fingerprint or device PIN instead of a password. Kithwall also uses it to unlock your encryption keys on your device, so there's no password to steal or forget. Add more passkeys (for example on a second phone) in [Security](/you/settings/security#passkeys).
help.signin.a2: Choose **Use a passphrase instead** when you join. A passphrase is a few unusual words only you know; it unlocks your keys the same way. You sign in with your @handle and the passphrase. No email address is needed.
help.recovery.title: Getting back in
help.recovery.a1: Twenty-four words that unlock your account if you lose every passkey or forget your passphrase. Save it in [Security](/you/settings/security#recovery-key) and keep it on paper somewhere safe. Making a new one stops the old one working.
help.recovery.q2: I lost my phone. How do I get back in?
help.recovery.a2: Go to [Recover your account](/recover), enter your @handle and type your 24-word recovery key. Then create a new passkey or passphrase. No email is needed — but anyone who has your recovery key could do the same, so keep it private.
help.recovery.a3: You choose 3 to 5 connections and how many of them must help. Your device splits your recovery key into pieces, one locked to each friend; a single piece is useless. If you need them, start from [Recover your account](/recover). After a waiting period (usually 24 hours) each friend sees **six words** and should approve only after hearing the same six words from you by phone or in person.
help.recovery.q4: Someone started recovering my account and it wasn't me.
help.recovery.a4: Every device where you're signed in shows a warning with **Cancel this request**. Cancel it and tell your trusted friends not to approve anything. Nobody can respond during the waiting period, and nothing can be unlocked without your friends.
help.people.title: Connections and circles
help.people.a1: Someone you've both agreed to connect with. Connections can see your profile and what you share with **Connections**. Requests appear in [Activity](/activity?tab=requests).
help.people.a2: A group of people, like Family or College friends. Each circle has its own feed, chat, albums, events and notes, and only its members can read them. Start one from [Circles](/circles).
help.people.a3: Only your connections, by default. Your name, photo and details are encrypted; Kithwall's servers only see your @handle.
help.sharing.title: Posts, stories and notes
help.sharing.a1: Photos or short updates that disappear after 24 hours. Share them with all your connections or one circle from the top of [Home](/home).
help.sharing.a2: Only you see how many people liked your post. There are no public like counts, and Home is in time order: no algorithm decides what you see.
help.sharing.a3: Longer writing — letters, recipes, journals — with simple formatting. Write one from [Notes](/notes) and keep it to yourself or share it with your connections or a circle.
help.privacy.title: Encryption and privacy
help.privacy.a1: Your posts, photos, comments, messages, profile and circle names are locked **on your device** before they're uploaded, with keys only you and the people you share with have. Kithwall stores the locked copy but can't open it, and neither could anyone who stole our database.
help.privacy.a2: Only what encryption can't hide: your @handle, who is connected with whom, which circles and chats you're in and when, roughly how big things are, and your email address if you added one. The details are in the [Privacy Policy](/legal/privacy).
help.privacy.q3: What does “waiting for a key” mean?
help.privacy.a3: Keys travel from device to device. When you connect with someone, their app hands you their key the next time it's open. Until then you'll see this message; it fills in by itself.
help.safety.title: Safety and reporting
help.safety.a1: Your profile is visible only to your connections, read receipts are off, there are no public like counts, and people can only find you by your exact @handle or your invite link. Adjust these in [Privacy](/you/settings/privacy).
help.safety.a2: Use **Report** on any post, comment, message or profile. Because Kithwall can't read encrypted items, your device sends moderators a copy of that one item and the key that opens it, and they check it matches what's stored. The person isn't told who reported them. See the [Community Standards](/legal/community).
help.safety.a3: Blocked people can't see your profile or anything you share, can't message you and can't send you requests. If you were connected, blocking also removes the connection. Manage blocks in [Privacy](/you/settings/privacy#blocked).
help.safety.a4: Contact your local emergency services first. Then report the content so our moderators can act.
help.account.title: Your account
help.account.q1: How do I download my information?
help.account.a1: Go to [Data](/you/settings/data#export). Everything is decrypted on your device and saved as a file; nothing readable leaves your device.
help.account.q2: How do I delete my account?
help.account.a2: Go to [Data](/you/settings/data#delete). Deletion is immediate and permanent: your device confirms it with your identity key, then everything is erased. Backups age out within 7 days and can't be read because your keys are gone.
help.account.a3: Yes, and it always will be. There are no ads, no tracking and no paid tier. Kithwall is open source and will be funded by donations from the people who use it.
help.account.a4: Yes. All of Kithwall’s code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence, and [Help & about](/you/settings/about) links to the exact version that’s running. See [Donate](/donate) for ways to help.

safety.tips.sub: What Kithwall can and can't protect
safety.tips.pageBody: Short, honest advice. No app can protect you from everything.
safety.tips.passkeyBody: If your passkey syncs through iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager, that account can unlock your Kithwall keys. Protect it with a strong password and two-step verification, or use a passkey that stays on one device or a security key.
safety.tips.metadataBody: Kithwall can't read your posts, messages or profile, but its servers see metadata: who you're connected to, which chats exist and when messages are sent, your @handle, and when you're online. See "What Kithwall knows about you".
safety.tips.torBody: Kithwall doesn't keep IP addresses in its database, but your network provider can see that you use Kithwall. Tor Browser (or a trusted VPN) hides that and your location from both.
safety.tips.screenshotBody: Anyone in a chat can photograph or screenshot it, and the web app can't tell you. Share sensitive things only with people you trust, and use disappearing messages.
safety.tips.sharedBody: Don't choose "keep me signed in" on a device others use. Sign out or wipe it when you're done, and use a private window where you can.
safety.tips.notificationsBody: Notifications show who sent you something on your lock screen. Turn them off on this device, or hide sensitive chats, if others might see your phone.
safety.tips.recoveryBody: Before you rely on wipe or duress, save your recovery key somewhere safe away from this device, or set up trusted friends. Without them a wipe can lock you out for good.

transparency.t.reactions.label: Reactions in chats

transparency.t.friendships.label: Connections and requests

transparency.t.blocks.label: People you blocked

transparency.t.memberships.label: Memberships

transparency.t.audienceKeys.label: Keys shared with you

transparency.t.groups.label: Circles you created

transparency.t.events.label: Events you host

transparency.t.profiles.label: Handle and public keys

transparency.t.vault.label: Settings and private lists

transparency.t.push.label: Push notifications

transparency.t.nativePush.label: App notifications
transparency.t.nativePush.sees: For each phone with the app: its push address at Google, Apple or UnifiedPush, the public key notifications are encrypted to, and the app and system name.

transparency.t.checkins.label: Safety check-ins

transparency.t.checkins.hidden: The alert message, sealed on your device.
transparency.t.notifications.label: Notifications

verify.title: Verify safety number
verify.lede: Make sure nobody is secretly in the middle between you and {name}.
verify.qrLabel: QR code of your safety number
verify.qrCaption: Let {name} scan this code, or scan theirs.
verify.scannerLabel: Camera view: point it at {name}'s code
verify.saveFailed: That couldn't be saved. Try again.
verify.keyMoved: Their key changed while you were comparing. Compare the new number before verifying.
verify.noCamera: Scanning needs a browser that can read QR codes with the camera. You can always compare the digits instead.
verify.cameraDenied: Kithwall isn't allowed to use the camera. Allow it in your browser's site settings, or compare the digits instead.
verify.cameraFailed: The camera couldn't be started. Compare the digits instead.
verify.scanMismatch: The codes don't match. Don't mark {name} as verified: check you're both on each other's verify page, and if it still differs, someone may be in the middle.
verify.notKithwallCode: That isn't a Kithwall safety number code.
verify.compareBody: Read the numbers aloud with {name} in person or on a call you trust, or paste the number they sent you. Spaces don't matter.
verify.digitsMatch: The numbers match. You can mark them as verified.
verify.digitsMismatch: The numbers don't match. Don't mark them as verified.
verify.what1: Everything you share with {name} is encrypted with keys that live on your devices. This number is made from your key and theirs. If it's the same on both screens, you're talking to each other and nobody, not even Kithwall, is secretly in the middle.
verify.what2: Only you know who you verified: it's stored in your encrypted settings, not on our server.
verify.what3: If the number changes later, we'll warn you. It usually means they set up Kithwall again or recovered their account. Check with them before you share anything sensitive.
verify.storedNote: Verified {date}. Stored only in your encrypted settings.
verify.selfBody: Open this page from someone else's profile to compare your safety number with them.
verify.changedBody: You verified {name} on {date}, but their identity key is different now.
verify.changedVouched: Their old key signed the change, which is what happens when they recover their account. Verify again to be sure.
verify.changedUnvouched: The change wasn't signed by their old key. Check with them in person or on a call before you share anything sensitive.

calls.security.title: Call encryption
calls.security.code: Read these out to {name}. If they see the same emoji and number, your call is end-to-end encrypted with nobody in between.
calls.security.waiting: The safety code appears once you're connected.
calls.security.frames: Extra frame encryption is on: every sound and picture is encrypted again on your device before it leaves.
calls.security.dtls: Protected by WebRTC's end-to-end encryption between your devices. This browser can't add the extra frame layer.
calls.security.relayOn: Your IP address is hidden: the call goes through a relay that only sees encrypted data.
calls.security.relayOff: Direct connection: the people in this call can see your IP address. You can change this in Privacy settings.
calls.security.relayUnavailable: The relay isn't available right now, so this call may connect directly and show your IP address.
calls.settings.title: Calls
calls.settings.relay: Always relay calls (hide my IP from the other person)
calls.settings.relayBody: On (recommended): calls go through an encrypted relay, so the people you call never see your IP address, which can reveal roughly where you are. Calls may be a little less immediate. Off: calls connect directly when possible, which can be faster, but each side sees the other's IP address. The relay only ever handles encrypted audio and video.
calls.settings.saverBody: For slow, patchy or expensive connections (2G/3G, mobile data). Video starts small, voice uses about 12 kbps, and the people you call send you small video. You can also switch it on or off during a call.
calls.settings.camOff: Start video calls with my camera off
calls.settings.camOffBody: You can turn your camera on once the call has started.
calls.ended.relayBody: “Always relay calls” keeps your IP address hidden, so the call didn’t go ahead without the relay. Check your connection and try again, or turn the setting off in Privacy settings.
calls.ended.failedBody: Check your connection and try again.
calls.media.denied: Kithwall isn’t allowed to use your microphone. Allow it in your browser’s site settings (the icon next to the address), then try again.
calls.media.missing: No microphone was found. Connect one, then try again.
calls.media.busy: Your microphone or camera is being used by another app. Close that app, then try again.
calls.media.other: Kithwall couldn’t start your microphone. Try again, or test your camera and microphone.
calls.camError: Your camera isn’t available, so this is a voice call.

safety.bio.title: Unlock with biometrics
safety.bio.body: Use your fingerprint or face instead of typing the app PIN on this phone.
safety.bio.limits: Biometrics only ever open your real account, never the decoy. Your duress PIN still works on the PIN pad, so under pressure type it instead. If someone could force your finger or face onto this phone, leave this off.
safety.bio.needsPin: Set an app PIN first. Biometrics are an alternative to it.
safety.bio.unavailable: This phone has no fingerprint or face unlock set up.
safety.bio.invalidated: The biometrics on this phone changed, so biometric unlock was turned off. Use your PIN, then turn it on again.
safety.bio.lockout: Too many tries. Use your PIN.
safety.screen.title: Screenshots and app preview
safety.screen.body: Block screenshots and screen recording of Kithwall, and hide its content in the recent-apps view. It's off by default because it also blocks screenshots you take on purpose. Turn it on if someone else may look at or use this phone.
safety.screen.toggle: Block screenshots and hide app preview
safety.screen.iosHint: On iPhone, apps can't block screenshots. Kithwall hides its content in the app switcher and tells you when a screenshot is taken.
safety.screenshot.notice: Screenshot saved on this phone. Kithwall didn't tell anyone, but anyone who sees it can read what was on screen.
safety.recording.notice: Screen recording is on. Anything shown in Kithwall is being recorded on this phone.
keys.changedBody: {name}'s identity key is different from the one this device saw on {date}.
keys.changedVouched: Their old key signed the change, which is what happens when they replace their keys on a device they still have. Verify the new safety number if you want to be sure.
keys.changedUnvouched: Their old key did not sign this change. Until you accept it, Kithwall won't share new keys with them. Check with {name} in person or on a call you trust first.
keys.pausedVerified: Because you verified {name}, Kithwall won't share new keys with their new identity until you verify again or accept it.
keys.conflictTitle: Kithwall rejected a key for this chat
keys.conflictBody: Someone gave this device a key for this chat that its owner didn't make. It was not used. If you see this again, tell the people in this chat in person.
keys.pinBody: Lock Kithwall on this device with a PIN. It's asked every time the app opens and after it locks. It stops someone looking through your device, but if the device or a copy of its storage is taken, an expert can try PINs without any limit, so use a long one.
keys.pinHint: At least {min} digits; {recommended} or more is much harder to crack. Avoid birthdays and patterns.
keys.rememberedBody: Kithwall stays unlocked on this device. Anyone who gets this device or a copy of its storage could open your account, so turn this off on shared devices or if your device might be taken.
keys.limits: Honest limits: these tools protect you from someone looking through your phone. If a device is seized or copied, what the browser stored can be analysed and PINs guessed without a limit; if that is a risk, use the Kithwall app, a long PIN and your device's own encryption. Your account still exists on Kithwall's servers.
activity.type.security_notice: A new way to sign in was added to your account. If this wasn't you, check your passkeys in Settings → Security.
security.chatNeedsConnection: You can only start a chat with your connections, or with people in a circle you share who accept requests.
security.recoveryRequestActivity: Someone started recovering the account of {actors}. Only help if they asked you themselves, in person or on a call.
security.addLinkPreviewNote: Nothing is fetched until you tap. The link then goes through Kithwall's preview proxy.
security.linkPreviewFailed: Couldn't load a preview for that link.
security.chatLinkPreviewsBody: Shows an “Add link preview” button under links you type. Nothing is fetched until you tap it; the link then passes through Kithwall's no-log preview proxy.
keys.identityTitle: Kithwall didn't use a key from {name}
keys.identityBody: {name}'s safety number changed and their old key didn't sign the change, so keys and records signed with the new key were not used here, and anything they signed with it shows as unverified. Check with {name} in person or on a call you trust, then accept the new key on their profile.
keys.conflictTitleCircle: Kithwall rejected a key for this circle
keys.conflictBodyCircle: Someone gave this device a key for this circle that its owner or admins didn't make. It was not used. If you see this again, tell the people in this circle in person.
keys.unvouchedUnverified: Until then, anything signed with the new key shows as unverified.

security.roster.newBody: Admins can share this group's keys with new people. If you didn't expect this, check with the group in person before sharing anything sensitive.
security.roster.confirmBody: Sign {name}'s admin role with your key, so members' devices accept the keys {name} shares. Only do this if you made {name} an admin.
install.title: Install Kithwall
install.lede: Kithwall runs in your browser, so there's no app store and nothing extra to download. Add it to your home screen or computer and it opens like an app.
install.benefitWindow: Opens in its own window, straight from your home screen, dock or app list.
install.benefitNotify: Notifications for messages and calls. On iPhone and iPad they only work once Kithwall is installed.
install.benefitFast: Starts faster and shows unread counts on its icon.
install.benefitSame: The same Kithwall with the same end-to-end encryption. Installing it doesn't share anything about you.
install.accepted: Installed. Open Kithwall from your home screen or app list.
install.installedHere: You're using Kithwall as an installed app on this device.
install.pickDevice: Choose your device below to see how to install Kithwall.
install.ios.share: Tap the Share button in the toolbar (a square with an arrow pointing up).
install.ios.add: Scroll down, tap “Add to Home Screen”, then tap “Add”.
install.ios.open: Open Kithwall from your Home Screen. From there you can turn on notifications.
install.ios.other: To install on iPhone or iPad, open this page in Safari. Some other browsers also offer “Add to Home Screen” in their Share menu.
install.android.chromium: Chrome, Edge and most browsers: tap the menu (⋮), then “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”.
install.android.samsung: Samsung Internet: tap the menu (≡), then “Add page to”, then “Home screen”.
install.android.firefox: Firefox: tap the menu (⋮), then “Install” or “Add to Home screen”.
install.desktop.chromium: Chrome or Edge: click the install icon at the end of the address bar, or open the browser menu and choose “Install Kithwall” (in Edge it's under Apps).
install.desktop.safari: Safari on a Mac (macOS Sonoma or later): choose File, then “Add to Dock”.
install.desktop.firefox: Firefox can't install web apps on most computers yet. Kithwall works well in a tab, or you can install it from Chrome, Edge or Safari.
install.manual: Look for “Install” or “Add to Home screen” in your browser's menu.
install.native: Apps for Android and iPhone are on the way. Until then, the installed web app gives you the same private Kithwall.
install.nudge.title: Install Kithwall on this device
install.nudge.body: It opens like an app, starts faster and shows unread counts on its icon.
install.nudge.ios: On iPhone and iPad, installing is also what lets Kithwall send you notifications.
install.settings.title: Apps
install.settings.description: Install Kithwall like an app. Nothing extra is downloaded or stored, and it stays the same end-to-end encrypted Kithwall.

net.mirrors.body: Other addresses for the same Kithwall. If one is blocked, another may still work. Lists are signed by Kithwall, so a fake list is refused.
net.mirrors.none: No mirrors are known on this device yet.
net.mirrors.signin: Each address keeps its own sign-in. On a mirror, sign in with your passphrase or recovery key: passkeys only work on the address where you made them.
net.mirrors.qr: QR code with the signed mirror list
net.mirrors.shareIntro: Kithwall addresses (if one is blocked, try another):

net.mirrors.invalid.format: That doesn’t look like a Kithwall mirror list.

net.tor.title: Tor
net.tor.body: Tor hides which sites you visit from your network, and is very hard to block. It is slower.
net.tor.browser: Install Tor Browser from torproject.org (on a computer or Android) or Onion Browser (iPhone), then open Kithwall there.
net.tor.onion: Kithwall’s onion address (opens only in Tor Browser):
net.tor.bridges: If Tor itself is blocked, choose “Configure connection” in Tor Browser and use a Snowflake or obfs4 bridge.
net.tor.app.title: Use Tor (Orbot)
net.tor.app.body: Sends the app’s pages and messages through Orbot, Tor’s app for Android. Calls don’t go through Tor.
net.tor.app.needOrbot: Orbot isn’t installed. Install it from F-Droid or Google Play, start it, then come back.

net.help.title: If Kithwall is blocked
net.help.lede: Some networks block websites to stop people talking. Here is how to keep reaching your people. Whichever way you connect, everything you send stays end-to-end encrypted.
net.help.link: Is Kithwall blocked where you are? Here’s what to do
net.help.mirrors.title: Try a mirror
net.help.mirrors.body: Mirrors are other addresses for the same Kithwall, with the same people and messages. Share them as text or a QR code with people you trust.
net.help.tor.title: Use Tor
net.help.app.title: Use the Android app
net.help.app.body: The app can switch to another address by itself when the usual one is blocked, and can connect through Orbot.
net.help.vpn.title: A trustworthy VPN
net.help.vpn.body: A VPN can help, but the VPN company can see which sites you use. Choose a well-known, audited provider and be careful with free VPN apps. Some countries block VPNs too.
net.help.shutdown.title: When the internet is shut down
net.help.shutdown.body: If the whole internet is cut off, no online app can work, Kithwall included. Nothing already sent is lost: it waits, encrypted, until you can connect again. Agree on another way to reach your people before it happens.
net.help.safety.title: Stay safe
net.help.safety.body: Using these tools can be risky in some places. Only install Kithwall from addresses in a signed list or from people you trust, and check the app’s fingerprint.

links.warn.insecure: The connection isn't encrypted: others on your network can see and change this page.
links.warn.ip: The link uses a bare IP address ({host}) instead of a site name. Real sites rarely do this.
links.warn.userinfo: The part before “@” ({userinfo}) is not the site. This link really goes to {host}.
links.warn.mixedScript: The address mixes letters from different alphabets, a common trick to imitate a well-known site.
links.warn.confusable: The address uses letters that only look like ordinary ones. It may be imitating another site.
links.warn.mismatch: The link text says {claimed}, but it really goes to {domain}.
links.warn.shortener: This is a link shortener ({domain}): it hides where you will end up.
links.warn.deceptiveSubdomain: The address starts with another site's name, but it belongs to {domain}.
links.warn.long: The address is unusually long, which can hide where it really goes.
links.warn.obfuscated: The address is written in a way that hides where it goes.
links.warn.port: The address uses an unusual port ({port}).
